summary: HEATMAP, built by team VOLT for the challenge “Harmonization of MODIS and VIIRS hotspots,” is an interactive web globe for exploring NASA FIRMS fire detections in Pakistan from 2023 to 2025. MODIS and VIIRS detect fires at different pixel sizes, so raw counts are not comparable. HEATMAP draws all 233,816 detections as squares at their true pixel footprints, links overlapping MODIS and VIIRS detections as candidate co-observations, and compares both sensors side by side. Users can zoom, choose any date, and click any area for statistics. It uses archived data only; sensor calibration and live data are planned next.
details:
What it does: HEATMAP is an interactive globe for exploring NASA FIRMS fire detections in Pakistan, 2023–2025. MODIS and VIIRS have different pixel sizes (about 1 km versus 0.4 km), so raw counts can’t be compared. HEATMAP draws all 233,816 detections as squares at their true pixel footprints, which grow as you zoom. Users pick any date, click any area for statistics, and compare both sensors in a harmonization panel. It links overlapping MODIS and VIIRS detections (same day, within 60 minutes) into 3,863 candidate co-observation clusters.

Benefits: One common footprint basis for both sensors. It runs in any browser with nothing to install. All statistics use the complete archive, and users can download their view as a CSV. Limits are labelled on screen.

Impact: A first step toward one consistent fire record from both sensors. It helps researchers see where they agree and differ and helps communities and planners see past fire activity. Next steps are sensor calibration, live data and more countries.

Tools: NASA FIRMS data, JavaScript, React, Vite, Node.js, Map Libre GL, Natural Earth outlines, OpenStreetMap/CARTO and NASA GIBS base maps, GitHub, Vercel. Built on Windows computers, with Claude (Anthropic) assisting with code.

Creativity: Real pixel-size squares, coloring by sensor, outlined co-observations, a “Play months” replay and an animated smoke intro.
